title: Climbing Stairs
source: canonical Climbing Stairs concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Every move takes you up one or two steps. Return how many different orders of moves reach the top: one-then-two and two-then-one count as different orders.

examples.explanation: Two one-steps, or a single two-step.

hints: Think about the very last move: it arrived from step n-1 or from step n-2.
The counts follow the same rule one step back and two steps back, which is the Fibonacci pattern.
Iterate from the bottom keeping only the last two counts: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2).
solution: The number of orders for n steps is the sum of the counts for n-1 and n-2 steps, because the last move was a one-step or a two-step. Iterating with two rolling values: O(n) time, O(1) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include one step and larger counts where naive recursion doubles back on itself

visible.failNote: count distinct move orders, not move combinations
